newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Power NZ sees strong profit growth.
newsitem.headline: Power NZ sees strong profit growth.

text.p: Power New Zealand Ltd said on Thursday it expected the strong profit growth seen over the last three years to continue in the current year to March with further high population growth within its network.
Other elements would be synergistic gains from its 53 percent interest in Bay of Plenty Electricity and from the Rotokawa geothermal generation investment coming on stream.

Chairman Don Stanley said Rotokawa was running to budget and scheduled to begin its commissioning trials in early July. Stanley said it was too early to comment on the UtiliCorp United Inc -Mercury Energy plan to jointly control Power NZ.
Power NZ earlier reported a 20 percent rise in net profit before abnormals to NZ$55.32 million.
Net profit after abnormals, minorities and equity earnings fell to NZ$51.12 million from $64.95 million, but the prior-year number was inflated by the sale of Power NZ's stake in EnergyDirect.
Power NZ's total dividend for the year will come to 25 cents per share, equal to 74 percent of earnings and above the board's 60 percent policy.
Shareholders' funds, including minority interests, rose to NZ$709 million from $413 million.

The main reason for the increase was the revaluation of Power NZ's network assets to their current ODV (optimised deprival value), which generated a net credit of NZ$219 million to shareholders' funds.

"With our low level of borrowing, our current balance sheet shows the tremendous capacity which the businesss has to fund further growth at levels simlar to, or better than, those successfully achieved in the past year," Stanley said.
Shareholders were concerned that imputation tax credits be protected, given the notice of takeover from UtiliCorp and Mercury.
"However, I can give them an assurance that the board will monitor the situation closely and ensure that the value of imputation credits is projected in the interests of all shareholders," he said.
Power NZ last traded at NZ$6.20, up five cents.
